And during this same famine,
certain young men from the region of Gubos, Christians, rebelled in the island of 'Ibra, a village,
and they used to go out and take captives and kill their Christian brethren,
and enter therein and eat.
At this time, Theodore son of Kaloyan,
king of Nicaea, fell ill
in the city whose name is Nymphaion.
And when he perceived that he was dying,
he summoned to himself Patriarch Arsenios,
and to him he committed the care and upbringing of Kaloyan, his son,
because he was still small of stature.
For there was at that time under his authority a certain general named Michael, who was called Palaiologos.
And of him King Theodore was afraid,
lest he should meditate tyranny
and seize the kingdom with a violent hand—
which indeed happened.
Therefore he commanded one of the generals,
whose name was Gadinus,
to go to Thessalonica,
where Michael was,
and put him in irons,
and bring him to him.
Now when Gadinus went,
he said to Michael:
"I know that you will become king;
nevertheless, submit yourself shrewdly to bonds,
and come with me to the king.
And when he sees your submissiveness,
he will release you and magnify you."
And Michael did so,
and went to the king while bound.
And that king, when he saw that he did not complain,
trusted him, had compassion on him, and released him;
and he also made him a partner with the patriarch in the guidance of the boy.
And after a few days,
he departed from this life.
And Muzalon, his pro hexisemos (protovestiarios) {OCR?}, took him—
he who was also the son-in-law of Kyra Balouina {OCR?}, the king's sister—
and carried him to the monastery of Magnesia,
and laid him there in the tomb of his fathers.
And he tarried some days in that monastery, making a plot with his mother-in-law,
who was the sister of the king who had died,
so that he might become king,
and destroy the nobles who would not submit to him.
